settings.title: Blocked Drains in the Garden Route

settings.editor: Blocked drains can quickly move from a slow sink or bad smell to an overflow that disrupts the whole property. H2O Plumbers helps homes, guesthouses and businesses across George, Mossel Bay, Knysna, Oudtshoorn and nearby Garden Route areas with practical blocked drain clearing and clear next steps.

settings.title: How H2O Plumbers Clears Blocked Drains Properly
More than a quick poke at the pipe

icon_list.text: Check the symptoms: Slow drainage, smells, gurgling, outside gully overflows and repeat blockages all point to different possible causes.
Choose the right method: A simple blockage, grease build-up, roots and deeper pipe problems do not always need the same clearing approach.
Test the flow: Once the drain is cleared, the line should be checked where practical so the customer knows whether the issue looks resolved or likely to return.

settings.title: Blocked Drains Need Careful, Practical Fault Finding
A cleaner way to deal with messy drain problems

icon_list.text: Protect the property: Drain work can be messy, so the work area should be handled with care before, during and after clearing.
Explain the likely cause: Customers should understand whether the blockage looked like grease, roots, debris, misuse or a deeper pipe issue.
Prevent repeat trouble: If the same drain keeps blocking, H2O Plumbers can advise whether hydro jetting, inspection or pipe repair should be considered.

settings.title: Blocked Drain Questions People Ask Before Booking

settings.editor: Useful answers for Garden Route homeowners and businesses dealing with slow drains, smells, outside gullies, repeat blockages and blocked toilets.

items.item_title: Why does my drain keep blocking after I clear it?
Can H2O Plumbers help if an outside gully is overflowing?
Should I use drain chemicals before calling a plumber?
When would hydro jetting be better than basic drain clearing?
Do blocked drains need a camera inspection every time?

settings.editor: A drain that blocks again usually has a cause sitting deeper than the visible trap or toilet pan. Grease, soap residue, roots, debris, poor pipe fall or a damaged section can all create repeat trouble. Clearing the immediate blockage helps, but the pattern matters because it tells the plumber whether more investigation may be needed.

Yes. An overflowing outside gully can mean the branch drain or main property line is not moving waste away properly. H2O Plumbers can check the affected area, clear the accessible blockage where possible and advise if the symptoms suggest a deeper line issue or possible municipal-side problem.

Repeated chemical use is not ideal. It can be harsh, may not reach the real obstruction and can make the work area less pleasant or safe to handle. If a drain is slow, smells bad or keeps backing up, a practical plumbing check is usually better than adding more chemicals.

Hydro jetting may be a better option when the drain has heavy grease, sludge, debris or repeat build-up that normal clearing does not remove properly. It uses high-pressure water to clean more of the inside of the pipe, but the plumber still needs to decide whether it suits the line and the blockage.

No. A camera inspection is useful for repeat blockages, suspected root entry, cracked pipes, collapsed sections or unclear underground problems. Many straightforward blockages can be cleared without camera work, but if the same issue returns, inspection may help identify the real pipe condition.
